newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish share list fears impact of funds probe.
newsitem.headline: Swedish share list fears impact of funds probe.

text.p: The head of a non-official list of Swedish companies said on Thursday he was concerned about the effects the Morgan Grenfell funds case could have on the reputation of the Stockholm Borsinformations Aktelista (SBI).

The SBI is a 12-year-old list now with 20 companies that are not listed on the Stockholm stock exchange but are part of an alternative list that has cheaper costs, less need for records and falls under different taxation regulations.

Four of the companies on the SBI are found in some of the three European Morgan Grenfell funds that were suspended on Monday but reinstated on Thursday pending an investigation into possible irregularities.
"The talks about these funds and their unlisted elements can have a negative influence on our reputation in the shortterm," SBI owner Henrik Andersson told Reuters.
The companies listed on the SBI are Oxigene, Scala, Trio Information Services and Pricer - all of which have seen more active trade than normal this week.
Oxigene, Pricer and fellow SBI company Medical Invest are currently seeking listing on the Stockholm bourse.
Andersson said about 20 percent of Pricer's shares were held by a Morgan Grenfell fund.

Andersson pointed out that one of the Morgan Grenfell funds under investigation owned some shares listed on the Stockholm bourse, including Sintercast AB that has plummeted 40 crowns to 270 crowns by 1400 GMT Thursday.

"One should remember, however, that many of the Swedish shares found in the biggest of the funds, European Growth Trust, are traded on the Stockholm bourse which means the problem does not just have a bearing on the SBI," Andersson said.
Other Stockholm brokers said it was possible that Morgan Grenfell funds held other listed stocks.
But Andersson acknowledged that SBI, with an average monthly turnover of around 250 million crowns, was in a more precarious position than the stock exchange.
Andersson said it would be unfortunate for SBI if this affair resulted in a lack of confidence in non-officially listed shares.
"However we still don't really know so far what has happened in the funds Morgan Grenfell runs," Andersson said.
"We are a bit concerned ... but we think that this is not just a problem for our companies on the SBI."
The SBI is currently in negotiations with the Stockholm stock exchange to use its facilities.
